 Order

This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India while praying for following reliefs:-
(i) Issue a Writ, order or direction directing Clubbing and/or Transfer of all FIR's bearing No.660 of 2016 P.S. Harda District Harda dated 04.08.2016, FIR bearing No.103 of 2016 P.S. Pali District Umaria and FIR bearing No. 532 of 2013 P.S. City Kotwali District Mandsaur filed against the petitioner at various place in the State of Amandeep Singh Saran vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh

1 Madhya Pradesh before any Appropriate Agency/Court at one place as deemed fit by this Hon'ble Court.
(ii) Pass such other and further orders as may be deemed fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.

2. The facts as detailed in the petition reveal that various FIRs have been filed against the petitioner and company namely, HBN Dairies & Allied Pvt. Ltd. all over the country alleging that many people including the complainants in the said FIRs, had deposited money with the said company and the company had promised to return the double of the deposited amount within a specified time on maturity.
Thereafter, on maturity, when the said amount was not repaid to the people including the complainants, the aforesaid FIRs were registered as a result of which, the present petitioner was arrested.
The trial commenced in all the FIRs but at a slow pace and the company has repaid the amount to many of the complainants including other persons/depositors.

Certain FIRs in question were lodged at a time when company was in the process of closing down all activities pursuant to directions by SEBI and was cooperating with the SEBI and the SAT towards redressing the issue of repayment to its depositors and thus, there was no mens-rea of cheating or defrauding the depositors.
3. It is contended by the counsel that against the petitioner, the First Information Reports in respect of the above, have been lodged at various Police Stations in various State.
So far as, the State of Madhya Pradesh is concerned, the following First Information Reports have been lodged:-

2  A 4.

sentences.text: It is contended by the counsel that the aforesaid cases pertain to the same chain of transaction and the trial of the cases at different places will contravene the concept of speedy trial.
The present petitioner would not be in a position to defend himself properly as the trials are going on at different places.
It is further contended by the counsel that the petitioner had approached the Apex Court as well.

The Apex Court vide order dated 06.11.2023 in W.P. (Criminal) No.341/2022 contained in Annexure P/10, extended liberty to the present petitioner to approach the respective High Courts for the purposes of clubbing of the FIRs which have been lodged at different places in territorial jurisdiction of such High Courts.

It is contended by the counsel that the issue pertaining to clubbing of First Information Reports is no more res-integra and the same has been conclusively decided by the Apex Court in the case of Radhey Shyam vs. State of Haryana and Ors.

entities.text: Radhey Shyam vs. State of Haryana and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
. 
It is further contended by the counsel that the aforesaid decision has also been taken into consideration by this Court in W.P.No.23621/2023 (Devendra Kumar Shrivastava and others vs.
The State of M.P. and Others) decided on 21.09.2023.

entities.text:
W.P.No.23621/2023 (Devendra Kumar Shrivastava and others vs.
The State of M.P. and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it is contended by the counsel that in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court as well as this Court, all the First Information reports as detailed above, be clubbed and be directed to be decided by one Competent Court.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer and submitted that the present petitioner can very well appear through video conferencing but the clubbing of First Information Reports is not at all required.
It is contended by the counsel that the trial of the cases at a particular place, will also cause prejudice to the victims and other investors as well as witnesses.
6. No other point is argued or pressed by both the parties.

7. Heard the rival submissions of both the parties and perused the record.
8.
It is evident that the petitioner is seeking clubbing of the First Information Reports which are detailed in the memorandum of the petition.

It is further important to take note that the First Information Reports have been lodged with allegations that the money was deposited with the company and despite there being a promise to return the double, the same was not done.
The allegations in all the First Information Reports are almost identical.

9. The Apex Court in the case of Radhey Shyam (supra) held as under:-
"Following the exposition of this Court in Amish Devgan vs. Union of India & Ors.
reported in (2021) 1 SCC 1, we deem it appropriate in exercise of power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, to direct clubbing of all the FIRs, which can proceed together for one trial as far as possible, as we are of the opinion that multiplicity of the proceedings will not be in the larger public interest.

Amish Devgan vs. Union of India & Ors.
reported in (2021) 1 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We may hasten to add that all the states have no objection for abiding with such dispensation."

10. Thereafter again this Court in the case of Devendra Kumar (supra) held as under:
Amandeep Singh Saran vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32690115/
3

entities.text: Amandeep Singh Saran vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "On mature consideration of the facts and circumstances in the given case and the view expressed by the Supreme Court and the High Courts in above cited decisions among others, I find that for the complacency of not only the accused, but the sufferers clubbing of FIRs/trials would possibly ensure the speedy justice and it would also avert a situation of distinguished final outcomes of distinct trials.

Obviously, there appears to be a commonality of accusation with which the accused are charged with, therefore, rather to embark on different paths, it would be justifiable to navigate all proceedings in one direction to reach a solitary judicious conclusion.

Accordingly, I dispose of this petition directing respondents No.1 to 3 to issue appropriate direction to the police stations of different districts to transfer the FIRs (as detailed in paragraph 5.18 of the writ petition), fifteen in number, and club them together at a place where principal FIR bearing Crime No.895/2020 was registered at Police Station Kotwali District Morena.

Similarly, in those matters where the challan has already been filed in the Court and trial is triggered, such criminal cases shall also be transferred to the Court where cognizance of principal FIR is or to be taken.

Respondents No.1 to 3 shall also ensure issuance of requisite instructions to the police stations that in the event of receiving any complaint by the depositors/members against the petitioners, they should act as per the advisory issued and instead of arresting the accused (petitioners), notice should be issued to them vis-a-vis complaint made by the depositors/members to enable instant action for ventilating their grievance.
Let aforesaid exercise be completed by the respondents as expeditiously as possible.

"
11. In view of the aforesaid law laid down by the Apex Court as well as this Court, it is evident that in order to ensure speedy trial as well as effective opportunity of defence to the accused, it would be justifiable to club all three First Information Reports, together.

12. Accordingly, the First Information Reports lodged at Harda bearing Crime No. 660/2016 as well as Umaria bearing Crime No.103/2016 be clubbed together with FIR No.532/2013 with City Kotwali Mandsaur.
All cases ensued after lodging of the aforesaid First Information Reports, stand transferred to the competent Court, Mandsaur where the trial pertaining to FIR No.532/2013 is going on.

13. It is made clear that the Court concerned shall extend the opportunity of hearing to the witnesses and complainants to appear through video conferencing if they have any difficulty in entering their appearance personally.
14. The petitioner is directed to submit certified copy of this order before all three concerned Courts.
15. With the aforesaid, the present petition stands disposed of.
